messages:
alex: FYI customer reports chat session sends first chunk then nothing. SSE connection stays open; client sees no more bytes for 20-40s. They say localhost->proxy->our hosted endpoint. model: gpt-large, streaming via websocket.

maya: thanks. do we have their request_id or timestamp? also: which client (browser/node) and proxy (nginx/fastly)?

alex: customer provided tracer header: x-rd-request: rd-7a3b2c. client: react-websocket library in browser. proxy: corporate on-prem nginx reverse proxy.

maya: can you ask them to run a minimal curl reproduction (ws support is annoying, but SSE works similarly). request a curl to our /v1/chat/stream endpoint with headers and keep-alive. sample I usually send: 

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```

Please have them run with `curl -v` and paste first 60s of output.

devon: also ask for the browser console network tab capture (HAR) for the ws/sse request and any proxy/nginx access logs for the rd-7a3b2c request. if they can provide tcpdump/ngrep on the proxy that's golden.

nico: quick triage note: first-chunk-only symptoms often point to proxy buffering or `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` being collapsed. nginx sometimes buffers the upstream response and only forwards once buffer is full or request completes. we should check nginx `proxy_buffering` and `proxy_http_version`.

alex: customer uploaded a small debug bundle. logs-bot: bundle refs -> rd-7a3b2c-2026-03-12.tar.gz (link: https://uploads.example.com/rd-7a3b2c-2026-03-12.tar.gz)

logs-bot: extracted highlights:
- nginx access -> 200 for rd-7a3b2c, upstream took 0.15s to send first bytes, then no further bytes for 34s.
- application log at ingress shows keepalive open, no error from our end.
- tcpdump from proxy shows TCP window stalled after initial small packet (client not ACKing more?).

maya: interesting. could be client-side buffering too (browser sockets sometimes pause reading if JS thread blocked). alex, can you get a HAR and console stack traces? ask them to reproduce with raw node script (no browser) so we can isolate browser issues.

alex: customer ran node repro (attached in bundle). node repro uses `ws` lib to connect and prints incoming messages. They see the first event then socket data pauses for ~35s, then more chunks appear.

devon: since node repro replicates, that lowers chance of browser bug. next: capture ngrep on the proxy during reproduction: `sudo ngrep -W byline port 443` or tcpdump with `-w`. Also check nginx config for `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection ''; proxy_http_version 1.1;`

nico: on our side, check for any rate limiting or slow consumer timeouts in the runtime for that session id. alex, can you share full request headers (redact tokens) and `x-rd-request` present in our access logs?

alex: headers (redacted) pasted in bundle: 
```
:method: POST
:scheme: https
:authority: api.redwood.ai
:path: /v1/chat/stream
accept: text/event-stream
content-type: application/json
x-rd-request: rd-7a3b2c
user-agent: node-req/1.2.3
```

logs-bot: our access logs show request hit runtime node A, stream opened, first chunk logged at 12:03:21. subsequent token emits recorded but not forwarded to client until 12:03:56 (34s gap). tracing shows runtime queued outputs normally.

maya: putting this into triage: likely proxy buffering or TCP-level pause. next actions: 1) ask customer to test bypassing proxy (direct to api.redwood.ai) 2) provide tcpdump/pcap of the full session 3) share nginx config snippet.

alex: customer tried direct -> works (continuous stream). they confirm when curl -> direct endpoint they get steady stream. when going through their nginx it stalls.

devon: confirms nginx responsibility. ask them to set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off;` for that location and `proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding off;` then retest.

alex: customer applied config changes and reports steady stream now :tada:. they changed `proxy_buffering off` and removed any `proxy_buffer_size` small defaults.

maya: great. let's add a KB note for support: common symptom "first chunk then stall" often due to upstream buffering at reverse proxies (nginx, corporate proxies). recommended repro steps: 1) run curl direct vs via proxy 2) collect ngrep/tcpdump 3) check `proxy_buffering` settings + `proxy_http_version` and `chunked_transfer_encoding`. include sample curl above.

nico: I'll draft the KB entry and include nginx snippet. alex, please close with customer and confirm if they'd like config changes pushed to infra.

alex: customer happy, closing. thanks all.
